note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God, the adversary and the heavenly court are not pictured, Job, his wife and his friends are not portrayed as biblical people but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent or gruesome is shown (his sores are shown as bandages).
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures.

sections.meaning: Job still holds fast to his integrity after losing everything, and now the test reaches his own body: will a man still bless God when his own flesh and life are touched?
ideas: After the storm, in a field of blown-down trees, the one straight oak from before still stands upright, stripped and battered but unbowed
A grey-haired man stands straight and calm in front of his storm-wrecked farmhouse
A man's hand keeps its firm grip on a rope in driving wind and rain

A stethoscope is pressed to an older man's chest in a plain clinic

sections.meaning: Even when the one closest to him tells him to give up on God, Job takes the bad from God as he took the good, and does not sin with his lips.
ideas: In the ashes, his wife kneels beside him in tears, gripping his arm and pleading, while he looks back at her steadily and gently

A wife turns away in anger and despair at the door while her husband sits quietly
A man sits in the ashes and gives thanks over a single crust of bread
A field half in sunshine and half under rain, the farmer standing in the middle with open hands

sections.meaning: His friends come from far away to grieve with him, cannot even recognize him, and sit with him on the ground in silence, because his pain is too great for words.
ideas: Three men walk up a long dirt road toward a distant figure hunched alone in the ashes; the nearest stops with his hand over his mouth

candidates.prompt: After a great storm, a wide open field on a hill where every tree has been blown down and lies uprooted and broken on the ground. In the middle one tall oak still stands perfectly straight and upright: most of its leaves and many of its branches have been torn away and it is bare and battered, but it is firmly rooted and unbowed. The grey storm clouds are breaking up and clear daylight falls on the oak.

In the yard of a storm-wrecked farm, a grey-haired man in a plain work shirt stands straight and upright in front of his ruined farmhouse, its roof torn away, with broken fences and scattered boards behind him. His face is calm and steady and his hands hang at his sides. Overcast morning light as the storm clouds move away.

In a plain clinic room, a doctor in a white coat holds an X-ray picture of a man's ribs and spine up against a bright light box on the wall. A grey-haired man sits on the edge of the exam table in a plain shirt, looking at the X-ray with a grave, quiet face. Cool daylight from a window. The X-ray has no writing or marks on it.

On a small fishing boat riding low in a heavy grey sea, a grey-haired man is throwing his things over the side to keep the boat afloat: a suitcase is flying from his hands, and a television, a chair and boxes of belongings already float in the waves behind the boat. Stormy daylight, spray in the air.

A grey-haired man sits alone on the ground in a wide heap of grey ash where his house has burned down, a few blackened beams standing behind him. His arms, hands and neck are wrapped in white bandages, and in one hand he holds a broken piece of a clay pot, scraping it slowly along his bandaged forearm. His head is bowed. Dull overcast light, a few wisps of ash in the air.

In a bare hospital room, a grey-haired man sits alone on the edge of a hospital bed. His arms and hands, his neck and his bare feet are all wrapped in white bandages. His head is bowed and his shoulders slumped. Pale light from a window falls on him.

On the grey ash-covered ground of a burned-out home, a grey-haired man with bandaged arms sits quietly. His wife kneels close beside him in tears, gripping his arm and pleading with him, her face full of grief and despair. He turns to her and looks back at her steadily and gently, calm. Overcast daylight.

A close view of an old man's two weathered hands held out open, palms up, side by side. In one hand lies a ripe, glowing peach; in the other lies a sharp, thorny bramble twig. Both hands are held out in exactly the same way, receiving both. Soft daylight and a plain, softly blurred background.

Three middle-aged men in plain coats walk up a long dirt road toward a distant figure who sits hunched alone on a grey heap of ash beside a burned-out house. The nearest of the three has stopped with his hand over his mouth in shock, and another is starting to weep. We see them from slightly behind, at the side of the road, with the lone figure small in the distance ahead of them. Grey afternoon light.

Three middle-aged men in plain coats have stopped on a country road, staring ahead in grief at someone out of sight: one weeps with his face in his hands, one has his hand over his mouth, and one has let his travel bag drop into the dust. Grey daylight.

At a small country bus stop, three middle-aged men with travel bags, each just arrived from his own town, meet and embrace one another with grave, sorrowful faces. Plain daylight, an empty road stretching away behind them.

At night under a sky full of stars, four men sit silently on the bare ground in a small circle beside a grey heap of ash, with a single lantern on the ground between them. One of them, with bandaged arms, sits hunched; the other three sit close around him with their heads bowed, saying nothing. Seen from a low angle at their eye level. Quiet, still, deep blue night light.

Four men sit side by side on the bare ground beside a burned-out house in pale grey morning light, completely silent. The one in the middle, with bandaged arms, sits hunched; the others sit close against him with their heads bowed, their coats dusty. Seen from a low angle at their eye level.
